D. H. Lawrence, Women in Love.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/d-h-lawrence/women-in-love

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- D. H. Lawrence, the author, died 1930 (Wikidata Q34970, P570 = 1930-03-02).

First publication of the text used: 1920 (SE colophon: 'Women in Love was published in 1920 by D. H. Lawrence.'). The Wikipedia article on the novel says Thomas Seltzer published the first edition in New York City on 9 November 1920, and Martin Secker published a British edition in London in 1921.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in the United States on 9 November 1920, before 1931, so the US rule settles the country of origin too. A published work enters the United States public domain 95 years after publication, so this work entered it in 2016.
- Country of origin (United States, first publication 9 November 1920 in New York City): see the United States paragraph above. The 1921 British edition would also pass: copyright there lasts for life plus 70 years after the death of the author in 1930, so the work entered the public domain on 1 January 2001.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
